title: When the Kitchen Turns Again
premise: Ines Winterbourne, once a celebrated wedding planner and now the quiet owner of a small-town café, abandoned both love and his profession after a betrayal eleven years ago. When a water-damaged letter — written by him, never sent, postmarked the week he disappeared from Lila Moreau's life — surfaces during a renovation, it reaches her hands just as she returns to plan her own wedding in his town. Forced to cater the wedding of the woman he never stopped loving, Ines must decide whether loyalty to the friend who once destroyed his engagement matters more than the truth that letter carries. In the end, he speaks the rehearsed sentence aloud in front of everyone, Lila calls off her wedding, and the two of them plan one last event together: their own, small, imperfect, and finally believed in.
about_author: Ulyana Voss is a former pastry chef turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, because that's where she learned that people tell the truth when their hands are busy. She lives above her own café with a dog named Brioche and a firm belief that every ending should smell faintly of burnt sugar.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. We meet Ines in his café, meticulous, controlled, allergic to weddings, as he takes a catering contract for a society wedding to keep the business solvent. The emotional beat is quiet unease: the contract's venue is the same estate where his own engagement collapsed.

chapters.title: The Letter Behind the Wall
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. During a kitchen renovation, a plumber hands Ines a water-stained envelope postmarked eleven years ago — his own handwriting, addressed to Lila, never sent. He reads only the first line before he can't go on. The beat is dread: the past has a return address.

chapters.title: The Bride Who Used to Be Mine
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The client walks in for her tasting: Lila Moreau, his former fiancée, planning her wedding to a kind, ambitious man named Theo. Neither lets on they recognize each other at first. The beat is vertigo — Ines realizes the letter is now a ticking thing in his pocket.

chapters.title: What Marcus Knew
chapters.summary: Lila's POV. Lila, privately unraveling, visits her old friend Marcus — the best man whose interference ended her engagement to Ines. Marcus insists he acted to protect her from a secret Ines was hiding. The beat is poisoned loyalty: we learn someone lied, but not who.

chapters.title: Tasting Menus and Old Wounds
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ines and Lila work the wedding planning together, trading barbed courtesies that keep slipping into intimacy — a shared recipe, a laugh that lands too easily. The beat is dangerous warmth: they are falling back into rhythm neither can afford.

chapters.title: The Sentence He Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Flashbacks interleave with the present as Ines finally reads the whole letter: the truth he was bringing Lila on the night he vanished — that he had turned down her family's money and her father's ultimatum, and Marcus had told her otherwise. The beat is grief with a spine.

chapters.title: Theo, Who Deserves Better
chapters.summary: Lila's POV. Lila, days from her wedding, catches herself comparing every small kindness of Theo's to a ghost. Theo, perceptive, asks her directly if she loves him or the idea of rescue. The beat is moral weight: Lila must choose honesty over comfort, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus confronts Ines, confessing he sent the letter's lie to keep Lila from following Ines abroad — because he loved her too, and told himself it was protection. The beat is reckoning: Marcus offers to confess publicly, and Ines must decide if truth delivered by betrayal still counts.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. At the rehearsal dinner, Marcus stands to toast and begins his confession; Lila, seeing Ines with the letter in his jacket, stops him — she wants to hear it from Ines. In front of both families, Ines speaks the sentence he rehearsed for a decade. The beat is the floor giving way.

chapters.title: One Last Event
chapters.summary: Lila's POV, resolution. A year later: the wedding never happened, the café hosts a tiny gathering of forty people, no planner, handwritten vows, Brioche the dog as ring-bearer. Ines and Lila, co-owners of a rebuilt life, finally believe in weddings again. The beat is earned, unglamorous joy.
